questions.question_text:
The graph shown is best described as:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=5.6cm,height=5.6cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-3.4,xmax=3.4,ymin=-2.5,ymax=8.5,xtick=\empty,ytick=\empty,clip=false,xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,blue,<->,domain=-2.6:2.6,samples=80]{x*x+1};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Exponential curves have no turning point and are not symmetrical; this curve has both.
A straight line is not curved; this graph bends into a U-shape.

questions.solution_text: The graph is a symmetrical U-shape with a single turning point, so it is a **parabola**.

questions.question_text:
The graph shown is best described as:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=5.6cm,height=5.6cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-3.4,xmax=3.4,ymin=-1.5,ymax=10.5,xtick=\empty,ytick=\empty,clip=false,xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,red,<->,domain=-1.66:3.4,samples=60]{exp(-x*ln(4))};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: A parabola has a turning point and is symmetrical; this curve keeps falling with neither.
A straight line has a constant slope; this curve becomes less steep as it falls.

questions.solution_text: The graph falls one way with no turning point and flattens towards a horizontal line, so it is an **exponential curve** (decay).

options.why: Read the power as an $x^{2}$ term; here $x$ is the power, not the base, so it is exponential.
A straight line has $x$ to the first power only, not $x$ in a power.

questions.solution_text: $y=4^{x}$ has the variable $x$ in the power, so it is an **exponential curve**.

options.why: Exponentials have $x$ in the power; here the power $2$ is on $x$, so it is quadratic.
A straight line has no $x^{2}$ term; this equation does.

questions.solution_text: $y=x^{2}-5$ has $x^{2}$ as its highest power, so it is a **parabola**.

questions.question_text: Classify $y=8-2x$ as a straight line, a parabola, or an exponential curve.

options.why: There is no $x^{2}$ term; the highest power of $x$ is $1$, so the graph is not curved.
The variable $x$ is not in a power, so the relationship is not exponential.

questions.solution_text: The highest power of $x$ is $1$, so $y=8-2x$ is linear — a **straight line**.

options.why: The outer power is $2$, a fixed index on a bracket, not the variable $x$ in the power.
Expanding the square produces an $x^{2}$ term, so the graph is curved, not straight.

questions.solution_text: Expanding gives $y=x^{2}+8x+16$, whose highest power is $x^{2}$, so it is a **parabola**.

questions.question_text: A curve has no turning point and levels off towards a horizontal line it never reaches. The curve is:

options.why: A parabola has a turning point and no horizontal line it approaches.
A straight line does not level off; it keeps the same slope forever.

questions.solution_text: No turning point and flattening towards a horizontal line are the features of an **exponential curve**.

questions.question_text:
Which equation matches the graph shown?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=5.6cm,height=5.6cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-3.4,xmax=3.4,ymin=-2.5,ymax=7.5,xtick=\empty,ytick=\empty,clip=false,xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,blue,<->,domain=-2.9:2.9,samples=80]{-x*x+5};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: A positive $x^{2}$ coefficient opens the parabola upward; this one opens downward.
An exponential curve has no turning point; this graph has a highest point.
A reflected exponential lies entirely below the $x$-axis with no turning point.

questions.solution_text:
The graph is a parabola opening **downward** with its highest point at $(0,5)$, so the $x^{2}$ coefficient is negative and the constant is $5$.
$y=-x^{2}+5$
